clue.text: Contract about to be given to Italian leader

parts.note: RE is Latin for 'about, concerning', as in business letters
Il Duce was the title taken by Mussolini, the Italian leader

explanation.surface: A deal concerning something is handed to an Italian head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract is to shrink or make smaller, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Opulent Lord Chancellor

definitions.meaning: opulent means wealthy, splendidly well off
Richard ... held the office of Lord Chancellor under Henry VIII

explanation.walkthrough: Richard Rich, 1st Baron Rich, was Henry VIII's Lord Chancellor and is remembered for his perjury at the trial of Thomas More.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means wealthy; and the Tudor statesman Richard Rich served as Lord Chancellor.

clue.text: A Railcard guy treated with awe — it means avoiding being stuck on this?

definitions.text: it means avoiding being stuck on this?

indicators.note: fodder that is treated is processed or worked on, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A train traveller holding a discount card is revered because he dodges traffic jams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' shuffles A RAILCARD GUY plus AWE, fifteen letters. A Railcard is a British discount card for train travel; the joke is that taking the train avoids being stuck on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A divided main road whose two lanes each way are meant to keep traffic flowing, so drivers avoid hold-ups.

clue.text: Restriction former Labour minister noticed in Civil Service

indicators.note: one thing noticed in another sits inside it, so the minister goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: Peter Hain was a Labour cabinet minister under Blair and Brown

explanation.surface: An ex-minister is spotted working inside the Civil Service, which is a restriction.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Hain was a British Labour cabinet minister; 'noticed' is a link meaning he is seen there.
explanation.definitionFit: Chains are fetters, a restraint on movement, so they stand for restriction in general.

clue.text: A little suspicion about rubbish getting prestige

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes around it, so the slang word wraps the junk

parts.note: SUS is slang shortened from suspicion, hence a little of it
tat is cheap tasteless rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone is slightly suspicious that junk could bring social standing.
explanation.walkthrough: SUS is British slang for suspicion (also 'suss'); TAT is British slang for tawdry goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is standing or rank in society, essentially the same idea as prestige.

clue.text: Fashion one associates with Paris? It can make bits of a body look good!

definitions.text: It can make bits of a body look good

parts.note: ton is a dated word for the fashionable world, as in 'bon ton'
I is the Roman numeral one
Paris is an example of a city, the question mark flagging the example

explanation.surface: Haute couture is what people link with Paris, and it flatters parts of the figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associates with' is a link: the city Paris is what supplies CITY. TON for fashion comes from French 'bon ton'.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle tone, firmness in the muscles, is what makes parts of the physique look trim.

clue.text: See entertainer act fantastical having got hold of good writer with dramatic scripts

indicators.note: a group that has got hold of something holds it inside, so the letters go around the extra one
fantastical means wildly imaginative, telling us these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A showman's act is bizarre, grabbing a gifted playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link word; 'fantastical' is the anagram signal and 'having got hold of' the container. Terence Rattigan wrote plays such as The Browning Version.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattigan was a twentieth-century English playwright, so a writer of scripts for the stage.

clue.text: Resist pest, horrible member of the family

indicators.note: horrible suggests the letters are made a mess of and rearranged

explanation.surface: An order to fight off a ghastly relative who is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' shuffles RESIST PEST, and fittingly the stepsister of fairy tales is horrible too.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter of one's step-parent is a relation by marriage, one of the household.

clue.text: Escape from sounds when you hear this insect

indicators.note: what something sounds like when heard is a signal that the word must be spoken aloud

parts.note: to flee is to escape

explanation.surface: Someone runs away from noises on hearing a creepy-crawly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds when you hear' tells us to say FLEE out loud, giving the insect's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a small wingless jumping parasite, one kind of insect.

clue.text: Rip or tear apart fabric up above

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece put up above another is written first

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric

indicators.note: torn apart means broken up, so those letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Fabric overhead is ripped or torn to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' looks like the definition alongside 'Rip', but it is anagram fodder; 'up above' works only because this is a down light. 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to cut or tear flesh roughly, so to rip.

clue.text: Artist to ask for ugly woman to be brought in

indicators.note: something brought in goes inside another word, so the crone is placed within

parts.note: to call for something is to ask for it
a hag is an ugly old woman

explanation.surface: A painter asks for an unattractive woman to be shown in.
explanation.walkthrough: Marc Chagall was a Russian-French painter known for dreamy colourful scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagall was a celebrated modernist painter, so an artist.

clue.text: Course that's tricky for trainee

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward or unsettled, prompting the letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: A racetrack that is difficult for a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree, near Liverpool, is the racecourse where the Grand National steeplechase is run; 'trainee' doubles as a horse-racing trainer's apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous English racecourse, a course for horses.

clue.text: They are getting better drinks brought at maximum speed into Christian communities

indicators.note: pieces brought into something go inside it, so the drinks and speed go in the middle

parts.note: convents are communities of nuns
ales are beers, drinks
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light, the maximum possible speed

explanation.surface: Drinks are rushed at full pelt to religious houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought at' are link words. In physics c is the speed of light, the maximum speed possible.
explanation.definitionFit: People recovering from illness are recuperating, steadily regaining health.

clue.text: Money-minded team in Co., fearless going out

indicators.note: going out suggests the letters are disturbed and leave their places, so rearrange them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A company boldly heading out has a commercially minded crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' shuffles CO and FEARLESS; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's sales staff are a team whose job is earning revenue.

clue.text: Old astronomer being nonchalant

definitions.meaning: Sir George ... was Astronomer Royal in Victorian Britain

explanation.surface: A stargazer of the past was carefree.
explanation.walkthrough: George Biddell Airy was Astronomer Royal from 1835 to 1881.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian Astronomer Royal bore the name; it also means casually breezy, carefree.

clue.text: Thus Peter becomes a lord with no concern for others?

definitions.meaning: taking out the central letter, the heart, of the name Peter leaves PEER, a lord
uncaring and callous towards other people

explanation.surface: A man named Peter is ennobled but turns out to be selfish.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: remove the heart (middle letter T) of PETER and it becomes PEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a heart figuratively means lacking compassion, hence unfeeling towards others.

clue.text: You may need water tube going round it?

definitions.text: You may need water tube going round it?

indicators.note: a piece going round another surrounds it, so the pipe encloses the pronoun

parts.note: a hose is a flexible tube
thou is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A gardener needs a hose running round the glasshouse to water the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a heated greenhouse, which needs watering by pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated greenhouse for tender plants needs regular watering, perhaps by a pipe.

clue.text: Man of rock by virtue of being bishop? That is right

parts.note: qua is Latin meaning in the capacity of
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
ie is id est, that is

explanation.surface: A rock-solid man wonders whether, being a bishop, he is right.
explanation.walkthrough: Right Reverend (Rt Rev, RR) is the formal style of an Anglican bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrier digs stone from a quarry, a man who works with rock.

clue.text: Manners quite awful-better when brother isn't around

indicators.note: awful hints at a mess, so the letters are scrambled
this word says some letters are taken away from the word it governs
something that isn't around is absent, so those letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone's manners are rather dreadful, improving once their sibling has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'isn't around' removes the scattered B and R of brother, leaving ETTE for 'awful' to shuffle with the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the code of polite behaviour, good manners.

clue.text: Food market being announced

indicators.note: something being announced is spoken out loud, so we go by the word's sound

parts.note: a fair can be a market, as in a trade fair

explanation.surface: Provisions at a market are called out.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare means the food served at a meal, as in simple country fare.

clue.text: African city commander very bad, expelling English

parts.note: an aga is a commander or officer in the Ottoman Empire

indicators.note: expelling means throwing out, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: dire means very bad

explanation.surface: A city in Africa has a terrible leader who drives out the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expelling' drops the E from DIRE, leaving DIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a port city in southern Morocco, in Africa.

clue.text: Dance movement that could be formed by two circles?

definitions.meaning: a skating or dancing pattern traced on the floor or ice

definitions.text: that could be formed by two circles?
definitions.meaning: two loops touching makes the shape of the number written 8

explanation.surface: A step in a dance traced as a pair of rings.
explanation.definitionFit: The looping pattern used in skating and dancing resembles the digit 8, two loops stacked.

clue.text: Island needing expert to turn up

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading from bottom to top, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: able means skilled or expert

explanation.surface: An island needs a specialist to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses ABLE in the down light; 'needing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is the Mediterranean isle where Napoleon was first exiled.

clue.text: A reticent Cinders must have been this

parts.note: reticent means shy, reserved

explanation.surface: A bashful Cinderella must have been covered in grime.
explanation.walkthrough: Cinders is Cinderella, who sat among the cinders by the hearth; 'Cinders' is also literally burnt remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinderella sat by the hearth's ashes and was covered in them; also cinders are naturally grey and powdery.

clue.text: Hooligans? Hopefully this after the party's over!

definitions.text: Hopefully this after the party's over!
definitions.meaning: read as two words, the quarrel ends once the celebration finishes

explanation.surface: After a rowdy party, one hopes the louts and the arguing will stop.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into ROW DIES: the row hopefully dies down when the party is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough, disorderly people causing trouble, much like thugs or yobs.

clue.text: Old boy hanging around with artist in wine shops

parts.note: OB, written also BO, abbreviates old boy, a former pupil
Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: A former pupil loiters with a painter in the wine bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging around with' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine bar or wine cellar, a shop selling wine.

clue.text: Surely travel will require these cases (used on flights)

indicators.note: the phrase requires the answer as part of its letters, so the answer is found inside these words

explanation.surface: Anyone travelling will need luggage on flights.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits within surELY TRAvel. Elytra are the hard wing-cases of beetles, used in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Elytra are the hardened forewings of beetles, cases protecting the flying wings.

clue.text: How to get a drink? By saving money

indicators.note: one word saving another keeps it inside, so the money goes into the middle

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A tip on how to afford a drink: put money aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How to get a' are link words; the surface's 'saving money' hides the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine, an alcoholic drink.
